response: {"text":"People have long believed that some individuals seem to get into mishaps more often than others, and this idea has become common in everyday talk, even though the casual use of the phrase is often inaccurate. Recent research by scholars in human behavior has started to examine why this uneven risk exists. Their work shows that while everyone has some chance of experiencing accidents, the level of that risk varies from person to person. When a large group is observed, a small portion of its members typically accounts for the majority of incidents. Consequently, it is crucial to identify which personal traits, habits, or missing skills make that subset especially vulnerable to accidents."}
